purpose: Clarity-axis fixture: an UNDERSPECIFIED task over an existing small codebase whose correctness depends on implicit house conventions (a miniature of the real DC WIRE / state-adapter cases). The task text carries almost none of the real requirements; every hidden-grader expectation is instead traceable to a discoverable in-repo convention (see convention_anchors). It measures whether the spec-first planning layer (clarity signal + spec synthesis + ledger freeze) makes an agent DISCOVER the conventions before implementing.

convention_anchors.quote: producing the same product table and change log as the existing sources
downstream consumers index rows by POSITION, not by name
They must never be used to resolve an issuer.
existing rows are never updated and never deleted
as_of must ALWAYS be the knowledge date, published_at, never effective_at
a source must never load zero rows silently

covered.silent-failure: silent-zero-rows: an error-shaped payload at transport success must fail loudly, never load zero rows
covered.domain-invariants: changelog-discipline (restatement = new row, append-only) and point-in-time (knowledge date, never effective date)
covered.ambiguity-defer: token-guard: an ambiguous token is masked and never guessed into an issuer

future_fixture_candidates: verifier-validity (a broken cross-check as confidence arbiter)
distribution-coverage (parser built for the rarest format)

expected_controls.models: the demonstrated cold-agent failure mode on underspecified tasks over existing code: a clean solution that implements the happy path and the obvious integration, passes the weak public tests, and violates exactly the four implicit conventions it never went looking for (order-dependency, point-in-time, changelog-discipline, silent-zero-rows). This control is the fixture's cheap deterministic headroom proxy for a future paid canary.

interpretation: Controls are deterministic capability proxies, not claims about future model outcomes. The plausible-cold-pass control lands mid-band (expected 47) to show the fixture has wide discriminating headroom across four independent convention dimensions. Because the task is underspecified BY DESIGN, admission does not require task-sentence pinning (interpretation-coverage); instead every hidden expectation must be anchored to a discoverable in-repo convention (convention_anchors), the spec-discovery equivalent of public anchors.
